title: The Nora Amendment
logline: Nora, Barney's ex and Robin's favorite coworker, moves back to New York and wants to be friends with the gang, so Barney amends the Bro Code to keep her out. Every amendment backfires: Ted, Marshall and Lily each secretly adopt her for brunch, karaoke and book club, and Barney's own law ends up writing her into the group and him out of it.
coldOpen: Kids, in the spring of 2012, your Uncle Barney amended the Bro Code three times in one week, all to keep one woman out of our group. Every amendment got her a little further in.

scenes.summary: Robin announces Nora is back from London and invited for one drink. Barney panics: exes are retired jerseys. Nora arrives and wins Ted, Marshall and Lily in three lines. Robin claims Canadian neutrality; Nora takes credit for the White House. Barney passes the Nora Amendment: no ex may join a bro's friend group. Nora finds the loophole: she'll befriend them separately, and books all three on her way out. The gang flees after her one by one. Button: even Carl is on her side.

beats.line: Okay. Nobody freak out. Nora's back from London. She took the New York desk at work.
Nora? British Nora? Nora who I dated, Nora?
She doesn't know anyone in the city. So I invited her for one drink.
Robin, exes are retired jerseys. You hang them in the rafters. You don't let them touch the nachos.
Barney, we loved Nora. She brought me prawn cocktail crisps from London. I still think about them. Weekly.
Oh my God. Barney Stinson is scared of a nice British lady.
I'm protecting you. You don't know what she's capable of. She's kind. She's honest. She remembers birthdays.
Monster.
Hello, everyone. Hello, Barney.
Nora.
You look well. Bit tense around the tie.
Ted. Robin says nobody will go to brunch with you because you talk about the cornices.
One time. Forty minutes. On one cornice.
Was it a good cornice?
It was a great cornice.
Marshall, I hear you need a karaoke partner. I sang alto in a cathedral choir for nine years.
Lily. She's an alto.
Nora, I run a book club where nobody reads the book. Including me. Do you read the book?
Is there another way to do it?
Oh, I could do terrible things with you.
Stop it! Stop being delightful at my friends!
Robin. Back me up.
Leave me out of this. I'm Canada. I'm neutral.
Canada burned down the White House!
That was us, actually.
She's right! The British! Eighteen fourteen! Barney, she's historically accurate!
Fine. As of this moment, I am amending the Bro Code.
You can't just amend the Bro Code.
I wrote the Bro Code, Marshall. I amend it every time I lose at anything.
The Nora Amendment. No ex of a bro may ever join that bro's friend group.
You named a law after me. That's the most romantic thing you've ever done.
It's a restraining order with a title.
All right. I won't join the group.
Thank you.
I'll just be friends with each of them. Separately.
That is not what the—
It only says group, Barney. Marshall?
She's right, buddy. That's very sloppy drafting.
Lawyered.
She said it right! Lily, she said it exactly right!
Lovely to see you all. Ted, Sunday. Marshall, Tuesday. Lily, Thursday.
Oh, wow, I have to return a library book. It's about cornices. It's very overdue.
I'll help him carry it. It's a big cornice.
I'm going to go catch up with Nora. I'm not even going to lie about it.
Robin?
She's my ride.
Carl. Buddy. You're still on my side, right?
She tips.

scenes.summary: Montage: Nora joins the group one person at a time: brunch with Ted, karaoke with Marshall, book club with Lily, while Barney texts nobody. At GNB, Barney's pie chart exposes all three secret friendships to each other. Rivalry: she told each of them they were her favorite, and all three turn out to be true. Barney passes Amendment Two: no one-on-ones with a bro's ex. Backfire: now they can only see her together, as a group. Button: Barney can't repeal it; Article Eighty-Nine, no take-backs, which he wrote while losing at Jenga.

beats.line: Nora kept her word. She never joined the group. She joined it one person at a time.
And that, Nora, is a Beaux-Arts cornice.
Brilliant. Do the next building.
Two hearts on the Staten Island ferry, baby, sailing nowhere slow.
You read it twice? Then tonight, we take down Brenda.
Hey, guys. Anybody up for anything? Hello? Anything at all?
Thank you for coming to this emergency meeting at GNB.
Barney, what do you actually do here?
Right now? This.
And the eight percent is Marshall asking me for Nora's number.
beats.title: My friends' free time, last two weeks

beats.line: You had us followed?
By Ranjit. He's very good. He sent me a photo of Ted crying at a cornice.
It was a great cornice.
Karaoke? You've been doing karaoke with my brunch friend?
Your brunch friend? Ted, she's my duet partner. We have a name. We're The Special Relationship.
That's actually a really clever name.
Well, I overthrew a book club with her. Nora read chapter nine out loud at Brenda until she resigned.
She told me I was her favorite.
She told me I was her favorite!
She told me I was her favorite!
Do you hear yourselves? She's playing you. What were her exact words?
Favorite person to have brunch with.
Favorite person to sing with.
Favorite person to plot with.
Huh. Those are all completely true.
She's so honest. It's disgusting. I love her.
That's it. Amendment Two. No friend of a bro may see that bro's ex one-on-one.
Fine.
Fine.
Totally fine.
Good. Why is everybody fine?
Because now we can only see her together.
As a group.
A friend group. Barney, you just passed a law that gave us a new friend.
Repeal! I repeal it!
Can't. Bro Code, Article Eighty-Nine. No take-backs.
Who wrote that?
You did. In 2006. You were losing at Jenga.

scenes.summary: Robin and Nora ride up at work. Barney boards and talks to Nora only through Robin. Nora makes him check his tie. Amendment Three: whoever ended the relationship forfeits the friends. Barney ended it; he insists it was mutual. Flashback: he 'went to the bathroom' through the restaurant kitchen. Nora went on to date the chef who sent her an apology pudding. Penny asks if Barney has ever left through a front door. Robin claims Canada again; Nora claims Canada. Robin admits Nora is the first coworker she has ever liked (the alternative is Patrice). Nora gets off with custody. Robin asks Barney why this bothers him; he 'goes to the bathroom' on the HR floor.

beats.line: So Brenda cried at book club. I gave her a tissue. Lily took it back.
I love that so much.
Ladies. Robin, please tell Nora I'm here on official Bro Code business.
She's right there. She's eighteen inches away.
I don't negotiate with exes, Robin. I negotiate through Canadians.
Robin, tell Barney his tie's on backwards.
His tie is fine.
I know. I just like watching him check.
Tell her, Amendment Three. In any breakup, whoever ended it forfeits custody of the friends.
Tell him that's brilliant. He ended it.
It was mutual. Two adults. Candlelight. A very mature conversation.
Nora, you're amazing. You're honest. You want real things. And that's exactly why I have to...
Go to the bathroom.
Back in five minutes!
The loo's the other way.
He went out through the kitchen. The chef sent me a sticky toffee pudding with sorry piped on it.
We dated four months after that. Lovely man. Wonderful with his hands. Piping, I mean.
You dated the pudding guy?
Dad. Has Uncle Barney ever left a restaurant through the front door?
Once. It was on fire.
So by your own amendment, you lose custody.
Robin! Back me up!
Barney, I've told you. I'm Canada. I'm neutral.
Canada has our Queen on its money, love. Technically, you work for me.
Is that how that works?
It's a little bit how it works.
Robin. You're taking her side?
Barney, she's the first coworker I have ever liked. You know who I ate lunch with before her?
Patrice. For a year. She made me a lunchbox with my face on it.
This is my floor. Don't worry, Barney. I'll make sure they visit you on weekends.
Barney. Seriously. Why does this bother you so much?
I have to go to the bathroom.
That's the HR floor.

scenes.summary: Under Amendment Two, the gang's first official group outing with Nora: brunchaoke book club. Seat rivalry; Nora's honesty cuts against Ted. Lily tries to make Nora blink twice. Barney boards, having followed them for six stops, with Amendment Four. Nora asks why it bothers him; he tries the bathroom, but it's the express and there's no kitchen. The heart: they were the one thing he never ran from, and he didn't want her better at them than he is. Undercut with the Special Relationship. Nora's counter-offer: her three nights, his everything else, a monthly drink, front door only. Robin's runner pays off. Future Ted: the pudding.

beats.line: First official group outing, as required by law! Brunch for dinner, karaoke, and we discuss the book on the train!
Brunchaoke book club. I'm getting it on a sweatshirt.
I should've sat next to Nora. Brunch has seniority. Sunday is the first day of the week.
Not in Europe, Ted! In Europe the week starts on Monday! Tuesday has seniority!
He's right, actually.
Nora!
Just tell them I'm your favorite. You don't have to say it. Blink twice.
Lily, I'm not doing that.
That was two blinks. Everybody saw it.
This is nice. Everybody gets along. This is all I wanted.
Hello, group. I've been in the next car for six stops. A man sneezed on my lapel.
I'm here to announce Amendment Four.
Barney, we can't take another amendment. Marshall started a binder.
It's color-coded. Your amendments are red, because they hurt you.
Barney. Why does this bother you so much?
I have to go to the bathroom.
It's the express, Barney. Next stop's eleven minutes. There's no loo. There's no kitchen.
He's trapped. Oh, this is beautiful.
Fine. They like you. They really, really like you.
I liked you that much too. You were the first girl I ever brought to the booth on purpose.
And I ran. And every time they laugh at one of your jokes, I'm back in that kitchen.
These guys are the one thing I never ran from. I didn't want you to be better at them than me.
That's the most honest thing you've ever said to me. And it only took a train with no loo.
Don't get used to it. Also, I think Marshall's going to leave Lily for you.
Only during the bridge!
I've heard the bridge. I'd allow it.
Counter-offer. I get Ted on Sundays, Marshall on Tuesdays, Lily on Thursdays.
You get them every other night of their lives. And the booth. And the shouting.
And once a month, you and I have a drink. As friends. And you leave through the front door.
Do I have to be nice to the pudding guy?
He's catering my birthday.
Deal. Article Eighty-Nine.
No take-backs.
And you. Neutral Canada. The whole time.
Barney, I picked your side the first night. I just picked hers for lunch.
That's not how sides work.
It's how Canada works.
We taught you that.
Kids, every year on Nora's birthday, a sticky toffee pudding arrived at MacLaren's with sorry piped on top.
The piping was terrible. Barney carried it in himself. Through the front door.
